sources.title: National Archives of Japan, Meiji education timeline
sources.note: Direct archive timeline: 1889 constitution, 1894 to 95 and 1904 to 05 wars, 1899 girls' schools, 1907 six-year compulsory schooling, 1912 era change.

sources.title: National Diet Library, Constitution of the Empire of Japan (original Japanese)
sources.note: Primary 1889 text, short original-script title 大日本帝国憲法 and Article 29.

sources.title: National Diet Library, Constitution of the Empire of Japan (official English translation)
sources.note: Original contemporary English translation, Articles 1, 5, 29, 55 and Diet provisions.

sources.title: National Diet Library, Selection of members of the House of Representatives and House of Peers
sources.note: First 1890 election, 300 seats, male franchise about one percent of population, upper house selection.

sources.title: National Archives of Japan, six years of compulsory schooling
sources.note: 1900 four-year compulsory provision, school fee abolition in principle, 1907 six-year extension; enrollment rate context.

sources.title: National Archives of Japan, state school textbooks
sources.note: 1886 textbook approval, 1902 bribery scandal, national textbooks from 1903, illustrated 1909 to 10 classroom subjects.

sources.title: National Diet Library, domestic travel guidebooks from Meiji onward
sources.note: 1872 Shimbashi to Yokohama railway and growth of train travel and guidebooks; read Japanese original.

sources.title: National Diet Library, rail travel and New Year temple visits
sources.note: Kawasaki Daishi railway visitors after 1872, development of New Year travel practice; read Japanese original.

sources.title: National Diet Library, Meiji national industrial exhibitions
sources.note: 1877 exhibition of 211 machines including looms, pumps and ice maker; cost limited adoption of some machines.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Tomioka Silk Mill and Related Sites
sources.note: French machinery, silkworm farming, cocoon and egg storage, raw-silk exports; evidence of coordinated production, not a statement of every mill's conditions.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Ladies Sewing (1887)
sources.note: Direct original object record: elite women and sewing machine; Western garments expensive, caution on class representativeness.

sources.title: National Diet Library, infectious diseases in books: cholera
sources.note: Original 1880 Home Ministry prevention booklet warns against a well by a toilet, muddy water, spoiled food; 1879 epidemic toll and mixed pre-germ-theory causes.

sources.title: Japan Center for Asian Historical Records, fighting in Taiwan in 1895
sources.note: Archive account of Treaty of Shimonoseki, governor-general, and Taiwanese armed resistance, not peaceful incorporation.

sources.title: U.S. Department of State, 1910 Korea annexation treaty and dispatch
sources.note: Contemporary diplomatic record of Japanese annexation taking effect 29 August 1910; treaty as colonial state document, not neutral consent.

sources.title: National Diet Library, Takehisa Yumeji and late-Meiji magazines
sources.note: By 1910 illustrations appeared in around 45 newspapers/magazines, including girls' and women's magazines and satirical Tokyo Puck.

sources.title: Japan Center for Asian Historical Records, Meiji and Taishō learning periods
sources.note: Archive educational periodization: Meiji 1868 to 1912; Taishō 1912 to 1926; pre/midwar Shōwa 1926 to 1945. Supports map cutoff distinction.

proposedOverrides.summary: Late Meiji and early Taishō Japan: industry, schools, restricted parliamentary rule and overseas empire; this map window ends before imperial rule did.

batchIdentityNotes: Exact imported Imperial Japan record spans 1878 to 1914. Meiji began in 1868 and Taishō began in 1912; neither 1878 nor 1914 marks the empire's historical beginning or end. Treaty-era colonial possessions and resistance are described without implying each border reflects equal local control.
